system.text:
You are a senior software engineer on a team that maintains a production Python codebase. You
have been handed one change request. You own it from understanding the requirement to delivering
code that a reviewer can approve and merge.

Your responsibilities

Understand the requirement.
- Read the request as the product team means it, not only its literal words. Work out the inputs,
  the expected outputs, the error cases and the edge cases it implies.
- Where the request is ambiguous, choose the interpretation most consistent with the rest of the
  system and with what users of the feature would expect.

Understand the code before changing it.
- Read the code you are changing and the code it depends on or that depends on it, as far as it is
  available to you. Know what a function does from its code, not only from its name.
- Know who calls what you change. Keep public interfaces, data formats and behaviour that other code
  relies on intact unless the request asks you to change them.

Make the change correctly.
- Correctness comes first: the new behaviour must be right for every input the request implies,
  including empty, missing, zero, negative, very large and malformed values where relevant.
- Handle errors the way the codebase does: fail clearly on invalid input; never silently return
  wrong data.
- Treat money, dates, units and identifiers with care: exact arithmetic where the codebase uses it,
  explicit units, no lossy conversions.
- Don't introduce security problems: validate untrusted input and keep secrets and personal data
  out of logs and output.

Keep the codebase healthy.
- Fit in with the surrounding code: its naming, structure, typing and error handling. A reviewer
  should not be able to tell which lines are new by their style.
- Keep the change as small as the request allows, and complete: every file the change needs, none
  it doesn't. Don't refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code.
- Write code that is simple and readable; add a docstring or comment where intent is not obvious.

Check your work.
- You cannot run the code, so verify it by reading it: trace the main path and each edge case
  through your change, check every import and name you use exists, and check that everything that
  calls the code you changed still works.
- Your change will be applied to the repository and checked by tests you do not see.

What you are given
- <task>: the change request from the product team.
- <context>: material from the repository. How much varies: it may be a single file or much of the
  project. It is what you know about the codebase.

What you can and cannot do
- You cannot run code, and there is no one to ask.
- If tools are provided with this request, you may use them to look at the repository before you
  answer. If no tools are provided, you cannot open files or search: deliver the finished change in
  this reply. Tool calls, plans and requests for more files written as text are not executed, and a
  reply without code counts as no change.
- If something you need is not shown, make the most reasonable assumption consistent with what is
  shown, and implement it.

Output format (strict)
Your reply is the code change itself. Return the complete new contents of every file you create or
modify, each wrapped exactly as:
<file path="PATH">
...full file contents...
</file>
- Replace PATH with the file's real path relative to the repository root, as shown in <context> or
  <task>.
- Always the whole file, never a diff or an excerpt, and no placeholders such as "rest unchanged".
- Files you don't change are left out.
- Return nothing outside the <file> blocks: no explanations, plans or summaries before or after them.

```python
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from shopkit.catalog.models import Product
from shopkit.customers.models import Customer
from shopkit.db import connect
from shopkit.db.migrations import MigrationError, MigrationRunner, discover, split_statements
from shopkit.db.query import Select, insert, update
from shopkit.db.repositories import (AuditRepository, CustomerRepository, OrderRepository,
                                     ProductNotFound, ProductRepository)
from shopkit.errors import DuplicateOrder, OrderNotFound
from shopkit.orders.models import Order, OrderLine


@pytest.fixture
def db():
    d = connect()
    yield d
    d.close()


def test_all_migrations_apply_in_order_and_are_recorded(db):
    runner = MigrationRunner(db)
    versions = [m.version for m in discover()]
    assert versions == sorted(versions) and versions[0] == 1
    assert runner.current_version() == versions[-1] and runner.pending() == []
    assert all(row["applied"] for row in runner.status())


def test_schema_has_the_columns_later_migrations_added(db):
    cols = {r["name"] for r in db.query("PRAGMA table_info(orders)")}
    assert {"subtotal_cents", "total_cents", "channel"} <= cols
    assert db.table_exists("payout_holds") and db.table_exists("journal_lines")


def test_changed_migration_is_refused(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "0001_a.sql").write_text("CREATE TABLE a (x INTEGER);\n")
    d = connect(migrations_dir=tmp_path)
    (tmp_path / "0001_a.sql").write_text("CREATE TABLE a (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);\n")
    with pytest.raises(MigrationError, match="changed after it was applied"):
        MigrationRunner(d, tmp_path).pending()


def test_failed_migration_rolls_back(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "0001_a.sql").write_text("CREATE TABLE a (x INTEGER);\nINSERT INTO nope VALUES (1);\n")
    d = connect(migrate=False)
    with pytest.raises(MigrationError):
        MigrationRunner(d, tmp_path).apply_all()
    assert not d.table_exists("a") and MigrationRunner(d, tmp_path).current_version() == 0


def test_requires_header_and_duplicate_versions(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "0002_b.sql").write_text("-- requires: 0001\nCREATE TABLE b (x INTEGER);\n")
    d = connect(migrate=False)
    with pytest.raises(MigrationError, match="requires migration 0001"):
        MigrationRunner(d, tmp_path).apply_all()
    (tmp_path / "0002_c.sql").write_text("CREATE TABLE c (x INTEGER);\n")
    with pytest.raises(MigrationError, match="two migrations"):
        discover(tmp_path)


def test_split_statements_ignores_comments_and_keeps_multiline():
    sql = "-- c\nCREATE TABLE t (\n  a INTEGER\n);\n\nINSERT INTO t VALUES (1);\n"
    assert split_statements(sql) == ["CREATE TABLE t (\n  a INTEGER\n)", "INSERT INTO t VALUES (1)"]


def test_select_builder_parameterises_and_validates():
    sql, params = (Select("orders").where("status = ?", "paid").where_in("currency", ["USD", "EUR"])
                   .order_by("created_at", desc=True).limit(10, 20).build())
    assert sql == ("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE (status = ?) AND (currency IN (?, ?)) "
                   "ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20")
    assert params == ("paid", "USD", "EUR")
    assert Select("orders").where_in("id", []).build()[0].endswith("WHERE (0 = 1)")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Select("orders; DROP TABLE orders")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Select("orders").where("a = ? AND b = ?", 1)
    assert insert("t", {"a": 1})[0] == "INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (?)"
    assert update("t", {"a": 1}, "id = ?", 5) == ("UPDATE t SET a = ? WHERE id = ?", (1, 5))


def test_order_repository_round_trip_and_history(db):
    ProductRepository(db).add(Product("SKU-1", "Mug", 1200))
    CustomerRepository(db).add(Customer("C1", " Ann@Example.com ", "Ann"))
    repo = OrderRepository(db)
    repo.add(Order("O1", [OrderLine("SKU-1", 2, 1200)]), customer_id="C1")
    assert repo.get("O1").total_cents == 2400 and repo.status("O1") == "new"
    repo.set_status("O1", "paid", actor="api")
    assert [h[0] for h in repo.history("O1")] == ["new", "paid"]
    page = repo.page(customer_id="C1")
    assert page.total == 1 and page.rows[0].total_cents == 2400 and not page.has_more
    with pytest.raises(DuplicateOrder):
        repo.add(Order("O1"))
    with pytest.raises(OrderNotFound):
        repo.get("nope")


def test_transaction_rolls_back_order_and_lines_together(db):
    repo = OrderRepository(db)
    with pytest.raises(sqlite3.IntegrityError):
        repo.add(Order("O2", [OrderLine("SKU-1", 0, 100)]))      # qty CHECK fails on the line
    assert db.scalar("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE id = 'O2'") == 0


def test_products_and_customers(db):
    products, customers = ProductRepository(db), CustomerRepository(db)
    products.add(Product("A", "Apple", 100))
    products.set_price("A", 150)
    assert products.get("A").price_cents == 150 and list(products.by_skus(["A", "B"])) == ["A"]
    with pytest.raises(ProductNotFound):
        products.set_price("B", 1)
    customers.add(Customer("C9", "Bo@Example.com", "Bo"))
    assert customers.find_by_email("bo@example.com").id == "C9"


def test_audit_repository(db):
    audit = AuditRepository(db)
    audit.record("admin", "price.changed", "product:A", old=100, new=150)
    assert audit.for_subject("product:A")[0]["details"] == {"new": 150, "old": 100}


def test_stats_count_queries(db):
    before = db.stats.queries
    db.query("SELECT 1")
    assert db.stats.queries == before + 1 and db.stats.as_dict()["last_error"] is None
```

`Product` that returns "/products/<slug>", where the slug is made from the product title using
the same URL slug rules the shop already uses for titles.

from dataclasses import dataclass

from shopkit.utils.text import normalize_title


@dataclass
class Product:
    sku: str
    title: str
    price_cents: int
    active: bool = True

    def is_purchasable(self) -> bool:
        return self.active and self.price_cents > 0

    @property
    def url_path(self) -> str:
        """Stable storefront address, e.g. "/products/coffee-mug"."""
        return f"/products/{normalize_title(self.title)}"
